children: The Malaysian ringgit is expected to strengthen against the U.S. dollar into year-end, CIMB analysts say in a note. This is supported by a growing trade surplus led by electronics exports, foreign bond inflows and the seasonal conversion of export earnings into ringgit, they say. Continued investment in AI infrastructure should sustain demand for Malaysian electronics, keeping export receipts elevated despite an expected moderation in growth next year. Declining U.S. Treasury yields and a weaker dollar following the midterm elections are also expected to support the ringgit, they add. CIMB expects the dollar to trade at 4.00-4.10 ringgit through year-end, with a bias toward the lower end of the range. The dollar is 0.2% higher at 4.0554 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
